Cheaper sets don't work as well - I tried to save a few bucks by buying a cheaper set of these suspension rods. They worked okay for a short while but just couldn't stabilize large loads in the washer. The slamming resumed.

I watched a few online videos and found (according to a couple of videos I found online, so take it with a grain of salt) that it's not the springs that are the key to how these rods work. It's the cap on top of the spring. The cap has a collar that fits rather tightly on the rod and slides up and down, but with some resistance. Apparently that resistance is what provides the damping and stops the slamming. When that collar loosens over time and the cap slides too easily, the slamming starts.

I saw some innovative fixes. One was to use construction adhesive around the collar to increase the friction. Another was to put a small cable tie around the collar and cinch it tightly enough to increase it.

Or you could just buy this set of replacement rods. This set works. Washer is slamming no more. Several videos are available online that show how to install them.

I read up on this and here is the suggestion of experts for making good coffee with this method:

Rinse the #2 cone filter in hot water. Add 2 level or slightly rounded tablespoons of coffee per cup. A cup is 200 ml, or about 7.5 fluid ounces. (Adjust coffee-water accordingly if your cup is really a giant mug.) Bring the correct amount of water to a boil, then set it aside about 90 seconds to cool slightly. Add just enough water to wet the coffee. Wait a few seconds, then add all the water and give it one stir.

This makes a fairly strong cup. If you want a milder coffee, add a little water afterwards. If you use less coffee grounds the result will be weak and bitter.

Direct fit replacement. - I picked this filter up for use with my in-laws refrigerator. They've been going on 2 years now without changing the filter just because they never thought of a need to do so. Our family had been noticing that the water pressure for the in-door dispenser had been slowed to a slow trickle and that the ice was starting to have grains of who knows what in the cubes. I asked if they had changed the filter, and they were unaware that there was a filter to even change. Install was very simple. The filter was located in the upper right corner of the main compartment. To remove the filter, all I had to do was push in until I felt a click and pull the old filter out. I've use older style filters before with instructions to soak the filter for 30 minutes prior to install, but this one did not mention it. I removed the two plastic covers from the nipple end, lined up the plastic fins, and pushed the new filter in until I felt/heard a click. That was it......installed...... Next I ran the in door water for about 3 minutes or so to get all the air out the line and completely fill the filter as per the directions. I also tossed out the old ice so everyone could enjoy some fresh, clean ice. After about 10 minutes of work, we can all now enjoy better water pressure at the door with clean taste and clean ice. Great value for the price. Word of advise: I know manufacturers recommend replacing every 6 months, but save yourself some money and wait for an actual change in performance: pressure drop, change in flavor, or impurities in ice. You may find out that a filter can last longer than advertised.

So far 100% dust free - If I could get rid of all the the flex duct, I would…if I could find flex duct that that wasn’t thinner than tissue paper and more breakable than glass, I would. The problem is that is what is available.

So I searched for a way to eliminate bends, minimize the amount of flex, eliminate the possibility of clogging, and do everything I could to keep the lint and dust off the laundry room floor.

I liked the look of this product and with the exception of the depth of the fitting it worked perfectly. My dryer may be different than yours, but the frame of the dryer steps out (is deeper front to back) on the left side of the vent discharge. If the throat of the pipe had been a little longer or even perhaps adjustable (like pvc drain kits), then there would have been plenty of room and the dryer would not have interfered with the dust pipe . As you can see in the last picture, I had to place this piece on slightly at an angle. The part that allows the flex to attach to the elbow is brilliant. It softens the transition to the flex as well as prevent lint from escaping at the connection. The other thing this fitting does is extend back so that the flex pipe can’t be crushed.

I used a simple elbow where the pipe passes through the exterior wall. Now the short flex duct is straight with no bends. I used foil tape to secure the ends of the flex. It’s been a month or so, and so far no dust has escaped after numerous loads of clothes have run through the dryer.

This is definitely worth buying, and would be a 5 if the fitting was just a little longer. This project didn’t take very long and will save me from moving the washer and dryer and cleaning all the lint off the floor.

UPDATE 25 Feb 2017: as noted by other reviewers, even if you rinse this immediately after each use, this filter can become clogged after a bit. HOWEVER, IT IS NOT HARD TO CLEAN! Put 3-4 cups of water to boil in a pot on the stove (or fill the pot with hot water from your kettle to speed up the process). With the burner still on medium to medium-high, add 1 cup of plain white vinegar. Lower the coffee filter into the pot so that the drip end is at the bottom of the pot. Let it boil for a few minutes. Using the silicone tab, lift the filter out of the pot to see if the water is draining through freely. If not, continue to boil the filter until the water drains freely when you lift the filter out of the pot. Once it does drain freely, take the filter out of the pot, set it in the cup stand, and set the filter and stand in the sink. Pour the boiling vinegar water through the filter and let it drain out into the sink. Let the filter dry completely before the next use so that the vinegar completely evaporates. The filter is as good as new after this, and we don't taste any vinegar, either. But if you want to be extra sure, you can add a plain hot water rinse at the end of the process to wash away all the vinegar. ALL filters will clog after awhile, and cleaning them is a normal part of ownership.

A little messy, but works great! - My washing machine broke at the start of the recent quarantine, and I'm still waiting for an appointment to have it fixed. With most laundromats closed, in desperation I bought a Wonderwash, hoping it would tide me over until I can get my washing machine fixed.

This little machine is great! It is well-made and all the parts feel sturdy and high-quality. It arrives unassembled but is a breeze to put together, it takes five minutes and no tools. I highly recommend watching one of the instructional Youtube videos before doing your first load of wash, it explains the process thoroughly, but the basics are: determine load size, add a small amount of detergent and fill with hot or warm water to the fill line. Add clothes, tighten down the lid, then just turn the crank for two minutes or so (I time it by listening to a song on the radio.)

The key is to turn the crank slowly, not quickly, and let the wet laundry fall from the top of the chamber to the bottom with a good thud each time. This drives the water and soap through the clothes and cleans them thoroughly. Once you're done, drain the chamber using the supplied pipe, then refill with cool water to the fill line and crank for two minutes again to rinse.

My clothes came out really clean! Even garments with cooking stains washed right up. The only drawbacks are that water tends to splatter around a bit when you drain the chamber, and I found that to drain it completely when I was done I needed to turn the whole chamber upside down and let it set for a bit. I use the Wonderwash in my bathtub, so a little bit of water splashing around is not an issue.

Other than that, this is a perfect little machine for doing small loads of laundry. It was a desperation buy, but I am really pleased with it! After my main washer is fixed, I intend to keep it to use in my RV camper. It would also be great for dorm or apartment dwellers.
